body.statement: Can the handle \(\mathfrak H^{\mathrm{low}}\) exhibit constants \(\eta\in(0,1-2\alpha)\), \(\varepsilon_R\in(0,\min\{R_f,R_q\})\), and \(c_{\mathrm{sep}}>0\), and construct \(P_{0,n},P_{1,n}\in\mathcal M\) for all sufficiently large \(n\), with fixed \(p_x\), fixed positive \(f_x\), and fixed nonidentical asymmetric laws of \(U_1,U_2\) shared across \(j\in\{0,1\}\) and across \(n\), such that only the Bernoulli conditional means \(b_{j,n,x}\) differ; \(1/4\le b_{j,n,x}(a)\le3/4\) for every \(a\in\mathcal A\); \(\sup_x\|f_x\|_{H^{\beta}}\le R_f-\varepsilon_R\) and \(\max_{j\in\{0,1\}}\sup_x\|f_xb_{j,n,x}\|_{H^{\beta}}\le R_q-\varepsilon_R\); \(\operatorname{TV}(((P_{0,n})_{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n},((P_{1,n})_{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n})\le\eta\); and \(\|\mu_{1,n}-\mu_{0,n}\|_{L^{\infty}(I)}\ge c_{\mathrm{sep}}K_n^{1/2-\beta}\)?
body.justification: This fixed-nuisance Bernoulli modulus is the unresolved lower-bound headline. The moment restriction already supplies the protected neighborhood, so the question now isolates the genuinely new packet-construction and contiguity obstruction.
body.gap: Capitao-Miniconi, Gassiat, and Lehéricy perturb the latent density and separate in \(L^2\); no comparator fixes the density and two nonidentical asymmetric error laws while producing a valid Bernoulli marked perturbation with \(K_n^{1/2-\beta}\) supremum separation and an explicit \(\eta<1-2\alpha\) product-experiment total-variation bound.
body.consumer: An affirmative construction would combine with the all-honest-band testing reduction; it would yield a matching converse only after a future \(O(r_n)\) upper theorem is proved.

obligation.what_is_open: For compatible strict-interior quantitative constants, construct one fixed positive density and fixed nonidentical asymmetric error pair together with Bernoulli marked perturbations satisfying the range and strict Sobolev-slack constraints, achieving \(K_n^{1/2-\beta}\) separation, and having product-experiment total variation below \(\eta<1-2\alpha\).
obligation.obstruction: The enlarged index ranges still do not guarantee a nonempty strict-interior fixed-density submodel: necessarily \(\kappa|I|\le1\) and \(R_f\ge(2B_A)^{-1/2}\). For compatible constants, the remaining mathematical barrier is to build a single moment-annihilating packet that simultaneously preserves the Bernoulli range and Sobolev slack and then convert its factorial marked-channel attenuation into a weighted chi-square or Hellinger bound; the frozen core supplies no lower envelope for that conversion. The former \(c_0=1\) obstruction is obsolete because the moment condition now yields the protected neighborhood directly.
obligation.attempted: The moment inequality was used to derive a uniform protected neighborhood with \(\nu_*=(2M_e^{1/q_e})^{-1}\) and \(c_*=1/2\). The moment-annihilation route was then carried through the exact marked-channel factorization, giving factorial attenuation on a fixed frequency square. Direct compatibility checks isolate the remaining fixed-density obstruction, but the packet construction and product-Hellinger conversion do not close.
obligation.partial_result:
The moment condition itself supplies the protected neighborhood that was formerly assumed.  Let \(Q\) be either error law and let \(\phi_Q(t)=\int e^{itu}\,dQ(u)\).  Since \(q_e>1\), Lyapunov's inequality and the error-moment bound give
\[
 \int |u|\,dQ(u)
 \le \left(\int |u|^{q_e}\,dQ(u)\right)^{1/q_e}
 \le M_e^{1/q_e}.
\]
The inequalities \(|1-e^{iv}|\le |v|\) and \(|z|\ge 1-|1-z|\) therefore imply, for every real \(t\),
\[
 |\phi_Q(t)|
 \ge 1-|1-\phi_Q(t)|
 \ge 1-\int |1-e^{itu}|\,dQ(u)
 \ge 1-|t|M_e^{1/q_e}.
\]
Consequently, with
\[
 \nu_*=(2M_e^{1/q_e})^{-1},
 \qquad c_*=\frac12,
\]
one has \(\inf_{|t|\le\nu_*}|\phi_Q(t)|\ge c_*\), uniformly over the enlarged moment class.  Thus no separate spectral-modulus restriction, and in particular no endpoint obstruction involving an independently specified \(c_0\), remains.

Two necessary compatibility conditions for the requested fixed density remain.  The support and denominator conditions imply
\[
 1=\int_{\mathcal A}f_x(a)\,da
 \ge \int_I f_x(a)\,da
 \ge \kappa |I|.
\]
Moreover, since \(|\mathcal A|=2B_A\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 1=\int_{\mathcal A}f_x(a)\,da
 \le (2B_A)^{1/2}\|f_x\|_2,
\]
and hence
\[
 R_f\ge \|f_x\|_{H^\beta}\ge \|f_x\|_2
 \ge (2B_A)^{-1/2}.
\]
The displayed ranges of the quantitative constants do not themselves impose either \(\kappa|I|\le1\) or \(R_f\ge(2B_A)^{-1/2}\); when either fails, the requested fixed-density subexperiment cannot exist.

Conditional on compatible strict-interior fixed nuisances, moment annihilation gives the needed analytic attenuation.  Put \(h_n=f(b_{1,n}-b_{0,n})\), and suppose that
\[
 \int_{\mathcal A}a^k h_n(a)\,da=0,
 \qquad 0\le k<K_n.
\]
For \(|u|\le\Omega\), Taylor's formula for \(e^{iua}\), the support bound \(|a|\le B_A\), and the preceding cancellations yield
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |\widehat h_n(u)|
 &=\left|\int_{\mathcal A}
     \left(e^{iua}-\sum_{k=0}^{K_n-1}\frac{(iua)^k}{k!}\right)
     h_n(a)\,da\right|\\
 &\le \|h_n\|_1 e^{B_A\Omega}
       \frac{(B_A\Omega)^{K_n}}{K_n!}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
By the marked-channel factorization, the two-dimensional Fourier transform of the observed marked-density perturbation equals
\[
 \widehat h_n(s+t)\phi_1(s)\phi_2(t).
\]
For fixed error transforms supported in bounded frequency intervals, this transform is confined to a fixed square and inherits the factorial bound above.  What remains unproved is the simultaneous construction of a packet satisfying the Bernoulli range, strict Sobolev slack, and \(K_n^{1/2-\beta}\) supremum separation, together with a weighted chi-square or Hellinger inequality converting the Fourier attenuation into \(\operatorname{TV}(((P_{0,n})_{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n},((P_{1,n})_{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n})\le\eta\).
